title: The Best Charizard Cards to Collect — Every Era, Raw to PSA 10, Dated Sold Prices | Gengar's Collector's Desk
description: Gengar's pick of the Charizard cards that are true collectibles: Base Set (1st Edition, Shadowless, Unlimited), Dark Charizard, Shining Charizard, Crystal Charizard, Hidden Fates SV49, 151 Charizard ex, Mega Charizard X and Y, and the under-$50 shelf — each with dated raw, PSA 9, PSA 10 and TAG 10 sold prices and eBay links.
keywords: best charizard cards, charizard cards to collect, most valuable charizard cards, charizard card collection, base set charizard, shining charizard, crystal charizard, charizard ex 151, mega charizard x ex
intro: Charizard is the card that made this hobby. Every era since 1999 has printed one that collectors still chase, and most of the rest is filler with a dragon on it. These are the ones I'd put in the binder, from a $13 Radiant to a six-figure Crystal, with what each one actually sells for.
narratorNote: I'm Gengar. I haunt the Pokémon indices on this site and I've been through more binders than you've opened packs. The stats desk tells you what a card is worth today. This desk tells you which ones are worth wanting. Every number here is a dated sold price pulled from our own index data, never a listing. I don't tell you to buy anything — I tell you what the real collectibles are and let you decide.

shelves.label: The grails
shelves.blurb: The Charizards that define a collection. Vintage WOTC, one print run each, and nearly all of the value sits in the top grade.

entries.title: Base Set Charizard #4 (1999)
entries.why: This is the card. Holo, 120 HP, Fire Spin, the art every other Charizard is measured against. It is really three cards: 1st Edition (the black stamp, first print), Shadowless (no drop shadow on the art box, same early print without the stamp) and Unlimited (the one most of us pulled). Separate PSA labels, separate pop reports, separate prices — a collector picks one lane and knows which lane they are in.
entries.note: Per pokeinvest's pop read (Aug 20 2026) there were 123 PSA 10 1st Editions and 58 PSA 10 Shadowless, so the Shadowless 10 is the rarer slab even though the 1st Edition carries the bigger price.

entries.title: Crystal Charizard, Skyridge #146 (2003)
entries.why: Skyridge was the final set Wizards of the Coast made before Nintendo took the game back, and the Crystal Charizard is its secret rare: a holo with the Crystal Type mechanic on a card that most kids never saw in a pack. It trades almost only graded, so there is no clean raw price — which is itself the tell that this is a collector's card and not a player's.

entries.title: Shining Charizard, Neo Destiny #107 (2002)
entries.why: The first shiny Charizard in the English game, on a secret-rare slot in the last Neo set. The foil is on the dragon itself instead of the background, which is why a clean one glows in a binder page. Every modern shiny Charizard — SV49, the shiny vaults, all of it — is an echo of this card. The 1st Edition print is the serious one; the Unlimited is the version you can still find raw.

entries.title: Dark Charizard, Team Rocket #4 (2000)
entries.why: Team Rocket's Charizard, drawn against a dark sky. Dark Pokémon were the first time the game let a card be a little mean, and this is the holo everyone wanted from that set. Same 1st Edition vs Unlimited split as Base Set, and the 1st Edition 10 has become a real auction card.

shelves.label: The centerpieces
shelves.blurb: Modern Charizards that already behave like collectibles: iconic art, a clear chase slot in their set, and a graded market deep enough to read every week.

entries.title: Charizard ex 199/165, Scarlet & Violet 151 (2023)
entries.why: The Special Illustration Rare from 151: a full-bleed painting instead of a framed card. This is the Charizard that brought a new generation into the hobby, and it is the heaviest card in our SV151 index. The grading value on modern SIRs sits almost entirely in the PSA 10, and the ladder below shows exactly how wide that gap is this week.

entries.title: Charizard GX SV49, Hidden Fates (2019)
entries.why: The shiny black Charizard full art from the Hidden Fates Shiny Vault. It sat in tins and ETBs for a year, got reprinted, and still never got cheap, because it is the modern descendant of the Neo Destiny Shining Charizard and collectors know it. The PSA 10 market on it is deep enough that we can mark it every week, which is rare for a card this old.

entries.title: Mega Charizard X ex, Phantasmal Flames (2025)
entries.why: The Mega Evolution era's Charizard. The Special Illustration Rare #125 is the art card and the biggest weight in our PF25 index; the gold #130 is the same Pokémon in the hyper-rare frame. Watch the grading gap: #130 sells for far less raw but more in a PSA 10, because the gold texture gems far less often.
entries.note: Per PSA's population report as read for our Pokémon knowledge base (Oct 4 2026), roughly 11% of graded #130s came back PSA 10 against about 60% of #125s.

entries.title: Mega Charizard Y ex 294/217, Ascended Heroes (2026)
entries.why: The gold hyper rare from this year's Ascended Heroes, and the Y form that collectors wanted after Phantasmal Flames gave us the X. Young enough that the 10s still come to market every week, which is the window for building a graded set of the Mega pair.

entries.title: Classic Collection Charizard 4/102 (2021 & 2026)
entries.why: The Base Set art, reprinted with a gold anniversary stamp for Celebrations in 2021 and again for the 30th Celebration this September. It is the way to own the 1999 artwork for under $200 without pretending it is the 1999 card. Searches collide with the real Base Set, so always put the set name in the query.

shelves.label: The starter shelf
shelves.blurb: Real Charizards for under $50 raw. Not placeholders — each one is the best Charizard in its set and a card a kid will remember pulling.

entries.title: Radiant Charizard, Crown Zenith #20 (2023)
entries.why: The shiny black Charizard in the Radiant frame, from the last Sword & Shield set. It is the cheapest card on this page that still looks like a chase card in a binder.

entries.title: Charizard VSTAR, Crown Zenith #19 (2023)
entries.why: Same set, the VSTAR. Pairs with the Radiant for a two-card Crown Zenith Charizard set.

entries.title: Charizard #14, Team Up (2019)
entries.why: A plain holo rare from Team Up. The PSA 10 is many times the raw price, which tells you how few of these were handled gently.

entries.title: Charizard GX #9, Hidden Fates (2019)
entries.why: The regular-art GX from the main Hidden Fates set, the affordable cousin of SV49 above. Same set, same era, a tenth of the price.

entries.title: Dark Charizard #21, Team Rocket (2000)
entries.why: The non-holo print of the Team Rocket Dark Charizard. Same art as the #4 holo, twenty-six years old, and still the cheapest way to put a WOTC Charizard in the binder.

collectingNotes.h: Know your print before you know your price
collectingNotes.p: Base Set Charizard is three different assets: 1st Edition, Shadowless and Unlimited have separate PSA labels, separate pop reports and separate price histories. The same split applies to Team Rocket and Neo Destiny. Our indices track each print as its own card, and the links on this page search for the exact print named on the row.

On modern Special Illustration Rares a PSA 9 sells for about what the raw card does; the premium is almost entirely in the PSA 10. On vintage WOTC holos the gap is wider still — a PSA 10 Base Set Unlimited Charizard has sold for well over twenty times the raw mark. That is why the raw column on a vintage card is a typical raw sale in any condition, not a near-mint price.

collectingNotes.h: Reprints are collectibles too — just different ones
collectingNotes.p: The 2021 Celebrations and 2026 30th Celebration Classic Collection cards carry the 1999 art with a gold stamp. They are honest, affordable ways to own the artwork, and they are not the 1999 card. Any search for "Charizard 4/102" without a set name will mix all three, which is why every link here names the set.

PSA 10 is the hobby's price reference and the price column you see most here. TAG grades by machine-measured imaging with human review and publishes a full defect report for every card, which is why we link TAG slabs beside PSA on every row. We think measured grading is where the hobby is heading — that is our view, not a price claim. How TAG grading works →
